lines.meet: I'm Freja, a midwife, or I was. When I tell you to do something in a fight, do it, and we'll argue about it afterwards.
lines.meet_neighbour: We're both in the Valley of Trials, aren't we? I'm Freja, the one in the infirmary tent who's never in it.
lines.ask_home: Quick, where are you from, before somebody starts bleeding?
lines.ask_work: What did you do before? I've guessed, and I want to see if I'm right.
lines.answer_home: Aarhus, in Denmark. Flat, windy, and everybody's on a bicycle, even in the snow.
lines.answer_work: Midwife, six years, mostly nights. Before that I played handball for twelve years on the pivot, which is where you take the most hits.
lines.chat_food: Rye bread with something on it, every meal, like a proper Dane. You've never had real bread until you've had Danish rye.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep in the day, mostly, from six years of nights. My body still thinks it's on shift at four in the morning.
lines.chat_missing: My husband's terrible jokes over breakfast after a night shift. They're worse than mine, and I miss them anyway.
lines.chat_here: Some people here think the Light makes them special. It doesn't, it makes them useful, and I've told two of them so to their faces.
lines.tease_quiet: You'd be wonderful on a labour ward, {name}, you're that quiet. The mothers would love you and you'd hate it.
lines.tease_talker: That's more talking than the whole of Denmark does in a year, {name}. It's a real record.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you'd count the contractions three times before you called anybody. Good, but I'd still shout at you.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you play like a handball pivot, all elbows and no plan. Come and play with me some time.
lines.tease_any: {name}, you're not bad at all, for somebody who argues with me. I'd still win, though.
lines.tease_back: Ha, that's a good one, {name}! I'll get you back, and I'll win.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's true, and I'll admit it, {name}. Don't make a habit of being right.
lines.bristle: Don't you dare, {name}. Not about that, not ever.
lines.apologise: That was too much, and I'm sorry. I don't always know when to stop.
lines.double_down: I meant it, and I'll say it again louder. You needed to hear it.
lines.needle_quiet: If you're bleeding, say so. I can't fix what you're hiding from me.
lines.needle_talker: Stop talking and do what I tell you. We'll argue about it after, I promise.
lines.needle_careful: You freeze when it matters, and somebody pays for it. You have to move.
lines.needle_bold: You think you're special, rushing in like that. You're not, you're just the one I've got to patch up.
lines.needle_any: You won't do as you're told when you're bleeding. That's the one thing I can't stand.
lines.bite_back: I've delivered babies in the middle of the night with nobody to help. Don't tell me I panic.
lines.hurt: Okay, that landed, and I'll think about it. Not right now, though.
lines.laugh_off: Ha, I played handball for twelve years. You'll have to hit much harder than that.
lines.confide: {name}, I'm frightened that one day I'll freeze at the wrong moment and somebody will die because of it. It's never happened. I'm still frightened of it.
lines.listen: I hear you, {name}. That stays with me, and I won't tease you about it, ever.
lines.look_out: {name}, stay where I can reach you in there. I'm faster when I don't have to run.
lines.accept: Fine, {name}, your way. Just this once, mind.
lines.deflect: Look after somebody who's actually hurt, {name}. I'm fine, and you know it.
lines.check_in: {name}, talk to me. What hurts, and how much, on a scale of one to ten?
lines.blame: Somebody didn't do what they were told in there, and it cost us. You know it was you.
lines.thank: You got me back up, and I didn't even see it coming. Thank you, properly.
lines.brush_off: That's the job, I'd do it for anyone. Lie still and stop arguing with me.
lines.worry: {name}, don't you ever do that to me again. Lie still and let me look.
lines.handed_down: It's only borrowed, this, because it was yours. You'll get it back.
lines.hand_fine: It's fine, you keep it. I've got my hands, and that's what matters.
lines.hand_sulk: Nobody asked me first, and now I'm annoyed about it.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, you're all right, you know. You argue back, and I like that.
lines.turn_friends: When it all goes wrong, {name}, and it will, you're one of the few I want next to me.
lines.turn_grating: I don't think we'll ever get on. Fine, I don't need you to like me, I need you to listen.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still heal you, it's what I do. Don't expect me to be nice about it.
lines.make_up: I've been impossible with you, {name}. I know I have, so let's stop.
lines.defend: Stop it, that's not fair. {name} did everything right, and I was watching.
lines.friend_left: {name}'s gone home for a bit, and now there's nobody worth arguing with.
lines.friend_back: Good, {name}'s back! I've got a list of things to argue about.
lines.common_medic: Six years as a midwife, mostly nights, being the calm one while something enormous happened. You've done that job too, being the calm one, I can tell.
lines.common_night_work: Six years of nights on a labour ward. My body still wakes up at four in the morning, ready for something.
lines.common_scandinavian: You're from up north as well! Danish, me, and don't you dare tell me Swedish is easier to understand.
